They made several attempts to that effect, and they usually mentioned the fact that it was their extremists, the extreme wing who wanted to do that. The extremists had been specifically tasked with that mission. They wanted to replace this Croatian lady and to bring Milovac Mile on that position, which was eventually done, and the funds from Sanski Most were then redirected to Banja Luka instead of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if you know, sir, can you tell us why the Serbs would want the money to go to Banja Luka instead of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: They were making preparations for the Autonomous Region of Bosnian Krajina or the actual Republika Srpska. Those were just preparatory measures, preparatory operations, and this was the final objective, and they needed money to finance that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could have the next item marked as the next exhibit. It's a document with English ERN 0306-5955.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P102.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, this is a document dated the 5th of March, 1992, bearing your signature as president of the Executive Board for the Sanski Most Municipal Assembly. Partly as a result of these violent actions against non-Serb properties and the incident regarding the head of the SDK, did the Executive Board take any action or reach any decisions that are referred to in that document?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, if it is going to be proper evidence in chief, the evidence should not be coming in a leading fashion from a leading question from Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I believe that was just calling for a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which does not necessarily make it -- makes it not leading perhaps, because also yes or no answer could be response to a question which is highly suggestive in terms of --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour, but I don't think it was in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but your response was just about the yes and no, which is not the entire answer. Let me just re-read the question. One second. Yes. A causal relationship is existing or not existing in the question, and if you would rephrase it in a more open way, that would be preferable. I remind you that usually leading questions, as such, not always opposed to but in certain circumstances where it becomes of more vital importance, then the other party can object against leading. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, can you tell us what that document is.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: This document contains the conclusions of the meeting of the Executive Board when measures were proposed following the incidents that had taken place over the couple of previous days. And the incident in question refers to the SDK. It was a case of vandalism. They simply wanted to remove the leadership of the SDK by force, and these are the measures that were proposed by the Executive Council at its meeting, the measures or the conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly, what were the proposed measures to be taken?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: See, we first condemned such behaviour on the 28th of February, 1992. That is what had happened at the SDK. We then offered a proposal whereby a change in the government should be done in accordance with the previous agreements following the multi-party elections, that is, there should be no forcible changes whatsoever as far as the SDK is concerned, that any personnel change should be carried out with full respect given to the people who had held this office before that. And this is what I wanted to say when I told you that the situation changed, that the circumstances changed over the time. We established the local government after the multi-party elections in 1990, but at one point the SDS wanted to have the National Defence Department, the Territorial Defence, the property department at all costs, which offices then at one point no longer were interesting for them. In turn, they became quite interested in the SDK. It must have been pursuant to a signal that had been given by someone from Banja Luka so that these funds could be redirected to Banja Luka. So they tried to achieve it by force, to implement it by force, so that the funds could be sent to Banja Luka. Because all of a sudden they changed their mind, and we no longer want this particular department, we want the public accounting service, because they could not get it through the regular agreements, and then they used "extremists," their extremist wing to implement this decision to take over the public accounting service, which they wanted at the time, and not some other department. And these conclusions listed under 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 are in response to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And some of those proposals for change to alleviate the situation, were they ever acted upon by the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Now, these were the times when we started expecting the worst. These are the first signs of lack of cooperation between us and the SDS. Before this happened, before this forcible takeover of power, that is when the proposal was offered to have Sanski Most declared Serbian Sanski Most and united with Banja Luka, so before that me and the president of the municipality, together with our associates, we would start working together every day at 7.00, drinking our morning coffee. We would agree on what we would do with that day, how we would proceed. It was a perfectly normal and collegial relationship, and we worked together during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, in --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In paragraph 12 of your statement, I believe you indicate that beginning in March and on into April of 1992, the main issue on the agenda as far as municipal business was concerned was an effort on the part of the SDS to have Sanski Most join the Republika Srpska and the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Now, I want to ask you about that. Did you have occasion to talk with Vlado Vrkes about why he and the SDS were so interested in making that happen?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: I think that it was either on the 6th or the 7th of April that we held the last session of the Municipal Assembly. At that time, during that session, they expressed their wish to place the proclamation of the Serbian Sanski Most on the agenda and also to declare the municipality of the Serbian Sanski Most part of Banja Luka region. Now, our response to the proposal was that if that should be the case, then we wanted to discuss the unification of the municipality of Sanski Most with Bihac. So we couldn't reach an agreement on that, so we proceeded with a break, and we established a commission which was supposed to come up with a proposal to be placed on the agenda of the session of the Assembly. However, no agreement was reached to that effect, and the session was never -- the session never resumed. As for the president of the SDS, I was on very good terms with him, and I put him in contact with a friend of mine from whom he had wanted to buy an apartment, and that is how he -- how he and I, after that session of the Assembly, this is how we met, Vlado Vrkes and this friend of mine from whom he wanted to purchase an apartment. But I don't know whether it was on the same day or the next day. If I may continue, please. I think that we thought that this would not eventually be placed on the agenda, the unification of the Sanski Most municipality with the Bosnian Krajina. And because we were good friends and we were close, I asked him, "How come that you want to place this on the agenda now, at this point, for the first time?" And he said that they had received an order to that effect in Banja Luka. He said that this was done pursuant to an order issued by Krajisnik, an instruction by Krajisnik. And then I asked him whether it was pursuant to an order by Brdjanin, but he didn't know exactly who was the person who issued the specific order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And after he told you this, did you discuss this with any of your fellow SDA representatives in the Municipal Assembly or the municipal government?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Now, what happened was that we did meet afterwards, but we didn't take his response to be sincere at the time. We thought that it was just a justification, an excuse that he had given for this proposal to be placed on the agenda, because after all, a long time had passed, and the Sanski Most municipality was then the last one in respect to which the proposal was made to be made part of the Bosanska Krajina region, and we concluded this must have been pursuant to a proposal that came from Banja Luka, because it was from that point on that bad things started to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this would be a good point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis. It's time for a break. Mr. Karabeg, your examination will be continued tomorrow at 9.00. Madam Registrar, that would be in -- Madam Registrar, I'm just checking whether we are in the same courtroom or not. But in whatever courtroom it will be, I would like to instruct you not to speak to anyone, not with the Prosecution any more, not with the Defence nor with anyone else, about the testimony you have given or you are still about to give tomorrow or the coming days.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll just try to find out where we're expected to be tomorrow. Yes. It will be in this same courtroom, Mr. Karabeg. Madam Usher, would you please escort the witness out of the courtroom. I would have one additional question for you, Mr. Hannis. Looking at P101, it very much seems a projected - please - it very much seems a projected map, because all the maps of Sanski Most -- well, look a bit different. A scale on it and a projected map certainly leads to all kinds of misunderstandings, so either we are fully aware that it's a projected map not giving the proper -- the proper relations between north, south, and east, west, distorted in that way. If that's clear, then we could work with it, but the scale is of no help. At least, if Merloit [phoen] is 1:300.000, is that the scale?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, which exhibit were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's P101, the coloured map with the--

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Ethnic composition?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. On the bottom it says Merloit, 1 to 300.000, and I perhaps a bit --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think as you described is our understanding. My purpose in showing that to the witness, Your Honour, was just to have him indicate that that map showed in general terms the location of various ethnic concentrations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- within the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And before we adjourn, may I raise one scheduling matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you make it quick because we have to leave this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I know. Based on earlier discussions that the week of June 7th was possibly a week that we would sit or might not sit, we have some witnesses scheduled for that week but it's important for us to know if that week is going to go off, then we want to cancel those people and cancel travel arrangements, but if not, then otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has not been able yet to give a decision on that and I call into your minds the meeting of last Friday which cast some light on why the Chamber was unable to reach any decision up to this moment. Then finally, Ms. Loukas, if we are confronted with the transcript tomorrow, would it be possible, especially if it would be a 92 bis (D), then of course we would have to decide whether it can be admitted under that Rule, could we have a copy this afternoon of the relevant part of the transcript you'd like to introduce with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Certainly. I take it then that -- therefore a decision has not been made at this stage as to whether to adopt that course or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think whether it will be under 89(F) or under 92 bis (D), I mean, one way or the other, I think we -- I have to discuss it still with the Judges, although my mind goes provisionally a little bit more in the direction of 92 bis (D) than in 89(F), but at least if it would be 92 bis (D), then of course we'd like to have seen the transcript in advance so we can take a decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Of course. Certainly, Your Honour, I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it could be delivered this afternoon. Thank you very much. We will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 25th day of May, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m.,
